title: The Brass Prototype
verdict: Bennett Wren was responsible for the disappearance of an anonymous source note.
intent: Bennett Wren wanted to prevent publication of a correction that would damage a favored candidate.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the managing editor handled the drawer key after the printer jam.
Remove an anonymous source note from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow ruler tube beside the layout desk.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: an anonymous source note disappeared from a campus newspaper office on election night.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the office printer jammed during the candidate-call rush.
The physical trace was thin paper strips under the layout desk.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a layout knife with paper fibers on the blade.
The item could be concealed in a hollow ruler tube beside the layout desk.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the managing editor knew the drawer could be opened by lifting the back rail.
The access pattern mattered because the managing editor handled the drawer key after the printer jam.
distractor_cues: a campaign volunteer hovering near the office
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
